normalized.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and hold ad costs near the pilot's 28% so it pays back by 2030
executive_summary: The US is worth entering: K-beauty skincare nearly doubled to $3.6B, and Onsoo's Amazon test sells (61% of K-beauty buyers buy mostly on Amazon; Pilot sales nearly doubled in six months)
Amazon-led entry fits the cash cap easily but pays back by 2030 only if ad costs stay near the pilot's (Payback needs ACoS of 28.6% or less; About $26M of revenue in 2030, not $40M)
Retail-led entry fails the board's tests even on the planning team's own inputs (Newcomers like Onsoo sell 2.6 units a door a week; Cash outflow passes the $18M cap in 2029)
A Japan scale-up is safer but adds only $7M of revenue in 2030, in a slow market (Japan pays back in 2029, with $1.8M by 2030)
Launch on Amazon in 2027 under an ad-cost ceiling; add retail only once awareness passes 20% (Ambition restated: about $26M by 2030)

slides.title: Entering the US market
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so by which route, within an $18M cash cap, payback by 2030 and an 8% group margin floor?
evidence: Success criteria: Cumulative US cash outflow of no more than $18M through 2030; Cumulative US cash back to zero by the end of 2030; Group operating margin at or above 8% in every year; A US business on the way to $40M of revenue by 2030; Only one major new-market launch in 2027
Decision maker: CEO and board of Onsoo Botanicals
Timing: Board meeting, March 2027
Out of scope: Mass-retail or DTC-led entry; US acquisition or distributor; US and Japan launches together in 2027

claims.claim: the 38% top of the benchmark range would raise the peak, still well inside the cap

slides.title: 2b: To pay back by 2030, Amazon ad spend must average 28.6% of sales or less, about what the pilot achieved

claims.claim: The threshold holds only if the plan's volumes do
evidence: Volumes are the planning team's: 300,000 units in 2027 rising to 1.1 million in 2030, with four more SKUs
Every SKU earns the hero cream's per-unit economics, as the planning team assumes

The pilot ran at 28% on a small budget; the scaling benchmark is 32%
A 25% duty adds $0.35 a unit

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and hold ad costs near the pilot's 28% so it pays back by 2030. Board decisions (March 2027): Approve Amazon-led US entry in 2027, with cash sized for benchmark ad costs; Restate the ambition as about $26M by 2030, on the way to $40M; Set the retail gate at Amazon sales above $10M and awareness above 20%; Decide on the Japan scale-up in 2028, once the US launch runs.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended: payback holds while ACoS averages 28.6% or less; fits cash cap (peak $3.2M at 32% ACoS) and margin floor in every case modeled; reaches about $26M revenue in 2030, short of $40M.

alternatives_considered.option: Option B, retail-led (national specialty retail) US entry
alternatives_considered.treatment: Reject: fails cash, payback and margin even on plan inputs; cumulative cash passes $18M cap in 2029, ends $20.8M down; margin below 8% in 2027–29; relies on 4.5 units/door vs 2.6 median and an unproven 1.3x halo.
Defer: safe, but leaves the US ambition untouched; adds $7M revenue in 2030, pays back in 2029, market growing 1.5% a year. Decide on Japan in 2028.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's retail trigger at 15% aided awareness and national specialty retail from 2029
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommend 20% aided awareness and test doors first, then roll out, with at least 4.0 units per door a week sell-through check.
Left out: not modeled by the planning team; the two channels carry 26% of K-beauty skincare sales against Amazon's 41%.
Left out: no inputs in the briefing pack; outside the options the board asked us to compare.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Payback by 2030 needs average ACoS of 28.6% or less; the plan assumes 25% falling, pilot ran at 28% on a small budget, scaling benchmark is 32%
The threshold holds only if the plan's volumes do: 300,000 units in 2027 rising to 1.1 million in 2030, with four more SKUs
Every SKU earns the hero cream's per-unit economics, as the planning team assumes
Duty stays at 15%; at 25% the threshold falls by about 1.5 percentage points; US tariff decision expected mid-2027
Ad cost at scale risk: −$4.7M effect on cash; tariff rise risk: −$1.1M; both together leave Option A at −$3.4M
Repeat purchase may stay at 29% as SKUs are added; not quantified; unclear whether more SKUs lift it
Korean-only labels may keep drawing complaints; not quantified
Exchange rate left out; a weaker won is upside only, so leaving it out is conservative
Four brands are a pattern, not proof
Amazon halo treated as a hypothesis to test, not a planning input
Model simplifications: one-time costs expensed when incurred; Option J cash equals operating result; tax, financing, exchange-rate moves and any value after 2030 left out
Aided awareness survey (1,200 US women aged 18–44) is narrower than Table 8's category buyers
